assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the three reviewed evidence items curated on blue-archive:aru@game at basis_commit: blue-archive:aru@game#chapter-1-checkpoint, the canonical MAIN_V001_C001 checkpoint, read in full; blue-archive:aru@game#character-state-ledger and blue-archive:aru@game#voice-address-ledger, the two active_provisional cumulative series-wide ledgers, read in their boundary, baseline and Chapter 1 (E008-E020) sections and in every entry that names Aru, including the Chapter 2 entries, which bound this assessment without extending it. All three are reviewed repository analysis of the pinned Japanese main-story text; the ledgers remain visibly provisional. The project's CURRENT_STATE_AND_CORPUS_MAP.md was read for method, authority order and scope only. Its PARTIAL_MODEL readiness census, the project reconstruction specification and bootstrap audit, the E008-E020 deep readings, the other five ledgers, group, bond, MomoTalk and event material and the Phase 3 packages are not curated evidence on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. No primary-source inspection, performed voice or adaptation is included.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Chapter 1 of the Countermeasures Committee arc only, BA:main:001:001:008 through BA:main:001:001:020 as reconciled at the MAIN_V001_C001 checkpoint, with the E020 chapter boundary as the default state: public post hoc ratification of the Shiba Seki demolition, the success-fee rule in force and the Prefect Team confrontation unresolved. The same ledgers record later Chapter 2 conduct (reciprocal alliance, reparation, refusal of former-client control) that contradicts a projection of this default, so no later state is established here, and no in-world calendar time is fixed.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: Checkpoint sections 9.1, 9.5, 10, 15 and 21 Reading E, with the state ledger's Aru row and its E015, E017, E018 and E019 deltas, support a bounded interpretation: the hard-boiled outlaw identity is aspirational and performative, the wish for freedom from constraint leads her to bind herself with a success-fee rule, and recognition by Mutsuki captures her into owning an act she did not intend. These are located literary interpretations of one chapter. No conditional rule set, motive weighting or response policy exists, and the checkpoint itself rejects any complete Aru model.

The state ledger binds a short sequence to units: E014 aspiration vocabulary, E015 freedom-from-law formulation, E017 operational success-fee rule, E018 friendship panic and shock at the demolition, E019 confusion then ratification. The checkpoint fixes the E020 boundary and lists her correction of the adopted culpability as open. The ledger's later Chapter 2 deltas show that boundary state changing quickly (reciprocity maxim, reparation, refusal of client control), so the sequence is a chapter-local trajectory, not a developmental model.

The voice ledger records located written forms for E014 (何事にも縛られない, ハードボイルドなアウトロー), E015 (法律や規律に縛られない、本当の意味での自由な魂), E017 (手付金はもらわない, 鉄則, 足枷, 成功報酬), E018 (友だちなんかじゃないわよぉーーーー！！, 一人前の悪党) and E019 (え……え？ before 冷酷無比！情け無用！), with the function of each. They support bounded canon questions about her compulsion-versus-freedom lexicon and performed villain register. The forms come from five units, the checkpoint warns that early speaker mappings cannot ground individual voice claims, E014 u:0039 is quarantined, and written register is not performed voice.

The evidence places Aru in the Shiba Seki restaurant and at a PS68 lunch, but analyzes those scenes for identity pressure, not routine. No Aru-specific account of ordinary habits, preferences or low-stakes conduct is established in the cited items; this gap says nothing about the character.

Checkpoint sections 14.6-14.8 and the ledgers distinguish her conduct by recipient: toward Haruka, rhetoric that an under-braked subordinate literalizes; toward Mutsuki, susceptibility to persona-confirming praise; toward the Kaiser PMC client, acceptance of work with little knowledge of him and a rule against advance payment; toward Abydos and the Shiba Seki proprietor, fear that hospitality will make everyone friends. The variation is located, but each relation rests on one to three units, and Haruka's recognition and Mutsuki's sincerity remain open.

E018's fear that staying at the restaurant will make everyone close and E019's cognitive lag (え……え？) before the outlaw register is reconstructed are the located interior evidence, with the checkpoint's judgment that villainy is aspirational rather than descriptive. Interior states are inferred from speech and reaction in two units; the E014 internal-monologue line is quarantined by attribution, and whether she privately recognizes the misunderstanding is listed as open.

Attested conflict conduct is a paid attack on Abydos coexisting with hospitality (E009), acceptance of a contract from a barely known client (E012), and in E019 challenging Abydos rather than correcting the command misunderstanding once Mutsuki supplies a villain framing. E020's engagement is analyzed for Abydos and the Prefect Team; Aru's own conduct there is not described. Local scenes only.

Located stances: outlawhood as freedom from law and discipline (E015), a success-fee-only rule chosen so that payment cannot become command (E017, in her own words), and public ratification of an unintended act in preference to truthful correction (E019). The checkpoint treats the rule as a genuine autonomy design and the ratification as persona capture. No deliberation on an unfamiliar moral question is shown, and her correction of the adopted culpability is an open question.

Her melodramatic villain performance and Mutsuki's teasing are analyzed by the checkpoint as the work's tonal method and as social pressure, not as an Aru humor or play repertoire. Nothing is established about how she herself jokes or plays.

The checkpoint covers twenty units with Aru present from E008, defers all contextual backfill and excludes PS68 private material; the ledgers state a 480-unit main-story boundary plus 3940 admitted supplementals, of which only the Chapter 1 entries fall inside this subject's curated coverage. The evidence is a chapter-local slice of a large corpus, and the deep readings that hold exact utterance locators are not curated on this subject.

Affirmative, located countercases: the checkpoint rejects the claim that Aru ordered the Shiba Seki demolition and the reading of her as simply a ruthless villain, citing her shock at the explosion, ratification only after Mutsuki's framing, self-binding rules and susceptibility to hospitality; the state ledger records that pre-blast intent to destroy the restaurant is contradicted, and its Chapter 2 deltas record reparation and refusal of renewed violence that contradict a projection of her outlaw performance. These are strong relative to the set's size but come from one project's own adjudication of one chapter.

Every claim is bound to a unit ID, the checkpoint's section 23 separates what PS68 knows from what the audience and Abydos know at the E020 boundary, and the ledgers preserve the knowledge available at each reading position rather than a consolidated endpoint. The state so fixed is immediately superseded in the same ledgers by Chapter 2 conduct, and no in-world dates exist, so the specificity is unit-level and chapter-local.

scenario_readiness.note: A dozen written forms from five units, two attribution quarantines and the checkpoint's warning about inconsistent early speaker mappings do not support new Aru lines; generated dialogue would be invention wearing the 鉄則 and 一人前の悪党 tics. The forms do support checking whether a proposed line contradicts her attested lexicon.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The E020 Chapter 1 boundary state, or one named unit from E008 to E019, with the Prefect Team confrontation and her adopted culpability unresolved.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: PS68 members (Mutsuki, Kayoko, Haruka), the Abydos Countermeasures Committee, the Kaiser PMC client or the Shiba Seki proprietor in their Chapter 1 relations.
setting_constraints: Abydos district contract, raid, restaurant or battlefield situations of the kinds narrated in E008-E020
No Chapter 2 or later development, supplemental story, bond or MomoTalk material

scenario_readiness.note: Even inside that scope the evidence supplies no application protocol, probe or rule set, and the ledgers show the boundary state reversing within the next chapter (reciprocal alliance, reparation). A novel situation can be checked against the located stances, not predicted from them.
No ordinary-life account exists in the cited items; readiness for a new mundane encounter is neither supported nor denied.

The located stances (freedom from law, the success-fee rule, ratification over correction) are described, but the checkpoint leaves open whether she corrects her adopted culpability and whether Haruka's misreading is recognized. A new ethical choice cannot be run; a canon question about those three stances can be answered.
Nothing romantic or relationship-intimate is established for Aru in the cited items.

conditions: Only PS68 contractor situations of the kinds attested: accepting a job from a barely known client (E012), refusing advance payment under the success-fee rule and stating its rationale (E017), and the command-ambiguity failure in which a subordinate acts on inferred desire (E018-E019).
Chronology is the Chapter 1 state; no later client relation or alliance is used.
Output is a behavioral tendency, not quoted dialogue, and retains the weak internal command-confirmation safeguard rather than a reformed organization.
The client's identity, PS68's economics beyond attested scarcity and any outcome after E020 end in abstention.
scenario_readiness.note: Her contractor conduct is the best-evidenced domain in the set: a stated rule in her own words with its reasoning, and one demonstrated failure of command clarification. That supports conditional tendency statements in that narrow domain and nothing broader.

known_limits.statement: The two ledgers extend to all 480 main units, and their Chapter 2 entries record Aru answering Abydos protection with 信頼には信頼で報いる, refusing renewed violence, leaving money for Shiba Seki repairs and rejecting former-client control; the Chapter 1 default state assessed here must not be presented as her later state, and those later entries lie outside this subject's curated coverage.

The checkpoint records inconsistent early speaker mappings and quarantined E019 and E020 attributions, and the voice ledger quarantines E014 u:0039; voice claims rest on clean lines only, and written Japanese register is not performed voice.

Haruka triggered the Shiba Seki demolition without an affirmative order; Aru's responsibility is post hoc public ratification, whose correction the checkpoint lists as open. Pre-blast intent to destroy the restaurant is contradicted.

Two of the three evidence items are active_provisional cumulative ledgers whose Aru content is unit deltas and one summary row; their provisional status and the checkpoint's deferral of contextual backfill mean no PS68 private, group or bond material informs the assessment.

The E008-E020 deep readings holding exact utterance locators, the other five ledgers, the project reconstruction specification and bootstrap audit, PS68 group and bond stories and the Japanese source itself are not curated evidence on this subject and were not used; missing support is not evidence of absence.
